findings.headline: DigitalOcean App Platform's ingress replaces ANY 5xx from the application with its own HTML page and a 504 status, dropping the body. The honest vendor-refusal state the dashboards are designed around cannot reach a client on DigitalOcean.
findings.whyItBelongsToThemNotHere: the two affected routes answer correctly and their code is not wrong; what has to change is how a DECLARED terminal refusal is carried, which is a dashboards design and instrument decision
findings.externalCorroboration: DigitalOcean's own App Platform feedback board carries the same behaviour with the same header: 'When a container on App Platform returns any 5xx response, the ingress replaces it with a generic HTML error page and a 504 status. The original status survives only as a response header ... Support confirmed this is enforced by the Cloudflare integration and cannot be changed per app.'
findings.remedyDirection: carry a declared terminal refusal on a status the ingress passes — a 4xx, as G-161's city_key_required already does — or on a header. G-152's Fire/EMS and Public works blocked boards, which name a vendor entitlement rather than a bug, depend on the client receiving that name.
findings.whatIsNotEstablished: the platform-internal reason the ingress treats all 5xx this way is described by DigitalOcean, not measured here; this lane measured that it does, on two apps, with x-do-orig-status=503 on the delivered 504.
findings.isItARegressionFromTheRepoint: no. It is pre-existing platform behaviour that was already true of walrus-app on the pin branch, because it depends on the platform and not on the commit. What the repoint changes is that the dashboards stop reading a host that passes 5xx through and start reading one that does not.

findings.headline: dolphin-app serves 3d3ec62, which still renders the FirstDue work-order free-text title where residents write names and phone numbers. main no longer does.
findings.carded: the planner's A-148 already records this and recommends shipping main; what this lane adds is that the recommendation is still unrled and that once D-13.1 is on main the ship must carry the base variable or fail closed
findings.notThisLanesCall: the dispatch conditions the ship on an operator ruling that does not exist

falsifier: This close would be falsified by any of: a feed returning a DIFFERENT RECORD SET (different record identities or a different record count) between walrus-app and GCP v1 rather than a live scalar or a replaced 5xx; services[0].source_commit_hash on walrus-app reading anything other than the main tip when read from the ACTIVE deployment; a public payload changing for a reason not on the G-159 list in the pre/post-repoint comparison; a G-159 route answering the SPA shell instead of 401 JSON from outside. Each was checked and each held: 0 unexplained of 20 paths on each public host, 9 of 9 comparable feeds matching by normalized hash, 2 differing scalars with both hosts stable within themselves, and 4 of 4 G-159 routes answering 401 JSON against a 200 SPA-shell negative control.
contradicted: Two expectations did not survive contact with the evidence, and both are stated rather than smoothed over. FIRST, the dispatch's framing that D-13 is a pure repoint — that every feed simply returns the same records through walrus-app as through GCP — is contradicted for two feeds, and not by anything in the dashboards or in smartcity-os: DigitalOcean's ingress replaces the application's own named 503 with a nameless 504 HTML page, so the dashboards' vendor-blocked state degrades in delivery even though the refusal itself is correct. That is now a carded finding and is the single thing in this lane most likely to surprise the next reader. SECOND, samsara/vehicles reported RECORDS-DIFFER, which reads like a data divergence between two clouds and is not one: with each host compared against itself as a control, both are stable and exactly two of 1189 scalar leaves differ (odometerMiles 10484/10483, safetyEvents7d 0/1). The lesson is that a hash difference on a live vendor feed is not evidence of divergence until a same-host control has been run.
missionPremise: OPS-17's G-159 close established that Bastrop's finance data is live in v1 and readable, and that two rows stood between it and a Bastrop staff member seeing it: D-14, because walrus-app built from side branch d9-api-8bea7fa so nothing merged to v1 main could reach smartcityos.io at all, and D-13, because the dashboards read every Bastrop feed from the GCP copy of v1 through a host hardcoded in five files. The dispatch holds both rows in one lane because the proof that matters runs across both — a repoint of the dashboards is only meaningful if the host they are repointed at is running main, and v1 running main is only meaningful if something reads it. The work rests on the dispatch's own re-measurement, not on this lane's assumption: read at source, main was one commit BEHIND the pin, so production was genuinely stranded.
completionPredicate: D-14 is DONE: main builds, starts and serves on a non-production DigitalOcean app; walrus-app runs main with source_commit_hash read back byte for byte; smartcityos.io and www serve the same payloads as before the repoint with every change attributable to G-159's four routes; deploy-on-push is off; the GCP smartcity-api is unmodified; and G-159's four routes are present from outside without a key (401 JSON) against an absent-path control (200 SPA shell). All of that holds. D-13 is NOT DONE, and what remains is nameable exactly: (1) the end-to-end leg on bastrop_tx through d12-main-uat is UNMEASURED because the G-135 verification-scoped tenant key has never been minted, and no substitute exists; (2) shipping main to dolphin-app is NOT DONE because no OPS-17 amendment dated 2026-09-18 or later records the operator's ruling, and the spec change it needs is written out above; (3) the platform's replacement of application 5xx responses means the dashboards cannot deliver two named vendor refusals on DigitalOcean, which needs a dashboards-side decision and is carded, not fixed. A successor should be able to close this row without re-deriving anything above.
scopeBasis: The boundaries are the dispatch's, and each exclusion is deliberate and named. Two repos and no more, in order, because the proof is one path. FAN-DEPTH 0 — no sub-agent was launched, so every measurement in this close was made by this seat and subAgents is {spawned: 0, maxDepth: 0}. The five dashboards data-source files are this lane's; src/server.mjs, src/compose.mjs, src/staff-map.mjs, the municode calendar files, web/app.js and web/index.html are G-161's and were not touched, which is why the shared d12-main-uat was moved and then re-measured against G-161's own contract rather than assumed intact. GCP was read and never written, because rule 3 keeps it as the rollback copy and the per-feed comparison needs it as the reference. getBnpApiKey() and server/routes/finance.ts were left alone because G-162 owns them and landing them first would make this repoint change behaviour when it must change none. The one thing this lane created, the d14-main-proof app, was removed after its commit was read back rather than left running with 39 production secrets in it; the leave_behind is declared as None with that stated, so a successor can tell a deliberate absence from an oversight.
